source: ClassPad.net Math — exact fx-880BTG PLUS, observed 2026-11-19 through visible keys and LCD SVG; saved directly to project.
notes: 67 native observations, all accepted full-LCD/status key replays, saved directly to project.

Variable grid retains natural radical and explicitly entered fraction values. sqrt(2) appears as sqrt(2), an explicit1/3 as1┘3, decimal0.5 and division1/2 as0.5, and pi/6 as a decimal. Explicit1/2 retains1┘2 even though decimal0.5 has the same numeric value.

Fraction representation propagates through an existing fraction variable (F+1 gives3┘2 when stored); copying a radical variable preserves its radical form. Fraction calculation objects are marked and propagated through variable/Ans references; decimal and pi memory paths retain numeric display. Native small radical, parentheses and fraction separator glyphs were sampled.

Editing A to7 leaves Ans/PreAns unchanged, independently probed as805 after inputs5,8. Variable editing error1/0 preserves draft and can be repaired to1/2; cancel/return restores the prior result. Storing the result into a variable also preserves PreAns: the same805 probe distinguishes the previous808 behavior.

CALC parameter entry uses linear expressions even with MathI output. Native roots are typed as sqrt(3 with omitted closing parenthesis, and fraction1┘2 is entered on a line. Forms retain radical/fraction memory presentation. A^2+C*3 evaluates3 at sqrt(2),1/3, then4 at sqrt(3),1/3 and9/2 at sqrt(3),1/2.

Cancelling pending CALC edits preserves the stored values; Run commits them. Opening VARIABLE from a CALC result ends the CALC session, so EXE afterward is a normal calculation. Four initially mislabelled CALC-fraction probes actually demonstrate this exit and ordinary fraction input; they were renamed, and the real CALC fraction draft/run were reobserved from a fresh form.
